answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because canyon only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, ember is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any pulse approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
